scope_note: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Markley Group's Lowell data center at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County. The selected IM3 footprint is one building inside a three-building assessor parcel, so every added value remains at campus or company/county scope and is unallocated to the selected building. State and City records add Phase I forecasts, cumulative investment, operating-headcount, TIF-savings and incentive evidence; the assessor and tax portal add annual real-property stocks and one complete billed-tax year; permit reports add discrete administrative construction values and contractor names; MassDEP adds a permit-listed generator count; and a recipient page verifies one community contribution. Forecasts, cumulative values, parcel stocks, billed taxes, permit values, permit-authorized equipment, white-space area and recipient funding remain distinct and non-additive. Searches of planning and permit files, incentive and compliance reports, assessor and fiscal records, utility and environmental materials, operator disclosures, contractor and supplier pages, workforce and procurement records, community recipients, archives and repository county panels found no audited annual construction outlay, construction workforce or payroll, vendor payments or local-purchase share, facility payroll, metered annual electricity, project-attributable utility upgrade cost, annual water series matching the evidence vocabulary, wastewater, actual emissions, cash tax receipts, marginal public-service cost, fiscal net or causal county outcome. No model is added because the missing allocation and expenditure anchors cannot be bounded defensibly and Markley is not a clean first data-center entry in Middlesex County.

project_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — selected building kept separate from the campus
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: IM3 inventory geometry and provenance; Markley current and archived operator pages; Lowell assessor parcel P90290/MBLU 184/4765/2; 2015, 2018, 2020, 2023 and 2024 City planning and bond records; deed/sale fields; and web archives. Exact identifiers included 2 Prince Avenue, 1 Markley Way, parcel 184/4765/2, assessor pid 47203 and IM3 source record 00214321737. The evidence supports a June 2015 purchase, Phase One open with customer occupancy by November 23, 2015, a three-building 14.4-acre assessor parcel, a later 65,000-square-foot expansion approval and continuing equipment changes. It does not map the selected 123,665-square-foot inventory footprint to an assessor building number or allocate campus investment, jobs, capacity, incentives or current white space to that polygon.
project_updates.project_description: Markley Group's Lowell data center operates at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County, Massachusetts, on the former Prince Pasta factory site. The selected IM3 footprint represents one building within a three-building assessor parcel, so campus-wide investment, employment, value, capacity, and incentive facts remain unallocated to that building. Markley reported Phase One open with customers occupying space by November 23, 2015 and now describes the Lowell facility as 352,000 square feet of secured white space. City planning records separately document a 2018 approval for a 65,000-square-foot expansion and later cooling, water-tank, generator, and utility modifications.

project_updates.title: Investment, incentive and fiscal audit — forecasts separated from cumulative observations
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: the 2015 EACC approval release; City TIF summaries and FY2020-FY2026 budgets; the 2023 preliminary official statement; EDIP awardee, annual-report, compliance and decertification pages; City Council packets; assessor history; and the Treasurer/Collector billing portal. FY2020 records the agreement as executed in May 2015, and the 2017 City summary describes a clawback provision and Middlesex 3 membership requirement; the signed agreement itself was not located. The fragment retains the $72.8 million Phase I plan, $104,121,860 cumulative-investment observation, $77,182,505 combined local incentive forecast, $187,500 approved state credit, $1,624,655.79 cumulative real-estate TIF savings and a separate $534,231.97 FY2026 real-property bill. Exact searches of adopted-budget documents 20496 (FY2023), 23767 (FY2024), 26555 (FY2025) and 30950 (FY2026 proposed) found no Markley row, and no 2021-2024 annual certified-employment table surfaced. The four FY2026 InvoiceCloud quarters are complete and show zero balances, but billed tax is not cash received and the portal does not identify adjustment versus payment. Partial FY2025/FY2027 displays are excluded; personal-property search returned no open Markley invoice and does not establish historical exemption value. The sources do not reconcile proposal vintages, prove credit use, publish annual realized abatements, allocate tax among jurisdictions, quantify public-service cost or support a net fiscal result.

project_updates.title: Assessor and parcel audit — four annual real-property stocks added
project_updates.notes: The official Vision Government Solutions Lowell portal was searched by Markley, Prince Avenue, Markley Way, parcel ID P90290, MBLU 184/4765/2 and property-record pid 47203. The card identifies Markley Group LLC, three buildings, 14.4 acres, a $3.85 million June 15, 2015 sale, and 2023-2026 total parcel values. The four total values are retained as one whole-parcel annual series. The sale price is not forced into an investment metric, individual building replacement-cost fields are not summed as economic activity, the 2026 value jump is not labeled new investment, and no selected-building, personal-property, payment or jurisdictional-distribution series was available from the card. The separate Treasurer/Collector portal supplies one complete real-property billing year and is not treated as an assessor value or cash receipt.

project_updates.title: Construction, suppliers and procurement audit — five issued permit values added without aggregation
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Lowell Planning Board applications, memoranda, plans and minutes; the public monthly issued-permit indexes for 2024, 2025 and January-June 2026; City online-permitting guidance; contractor and engineer portfolios; COMMBUYS and Massachusetts statewide IT contract records; tenant procurement disclosures; and archived trade coverage for 2015-2026. The City reports BLD202400574 at $3,350,000, ELC202406426 at $4,000,000, BLD202413857 at $15,538,186, ELC202507553 at $12,717,600 and BLD202603584 at $1,708,090. Each is retained once at its issue year even when later monthly reports repeat it as year-to-date or completion activity; related building, foundation and trade permits are not summed because scope overlap is unresolved. Exact searches of the relevant official reports did not locate third-party-cited ELC202409585, so its $19,076,500 figure is excluded. Named roles include Willard L. Cleveland, New England Electric Group and Markley Group Boston; the older contractor case study separately identifies Coordinated Systems Consulting and Saiful Bouquet. The CSS portal requires a registered login and the City page reports online permitting unavailable. No final contract amount, invoice, audited annual outlay, equipment-versus-building split, construction headcount, worker hours, payroll, residence, vendor payment or local-purchase share was found. Permit values are administrative estimates, not cash spending.

project_updates.title: Operations and workforce audit — dated headcounts and local-resident subset added
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Lowell TIF tables and annual certified-project reports; Massachusetts EDIP annual-report, compliance and decertification material; Markley careers, staff and facility pages; job boards; customer and tenant records; workforce-development, apprenticeship, local-hiring and wage-enforcement searches; and state procurement records for 2015-2026. No annual-average FTE, occupation table, wage, payroll, hours, apprenticeship outcome, contractor/customer headcount, turnover, county-resident total, procurement payment or selected-building employment was found.

project_updates.title: Resource, utility and environmental audit — permit equipment added; consumption remains unallocated
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: MassDEP air-plan applications, notices and OADR decisions under 24-AQ02F-0001-APP/NE-25-002, including the March 27, 2026 final decision and July 2026 reconsideration docket; Lowell Planning Board, Sustainability Council, water, sewer and data-center materials; fuel-storage licensing; National Grid and Massachusetts DPU dockets and tariffs; ISO New England queue and reliability material; EPA facility searches; Markley facility, PPA and sustainability pages; and 2025-2026 reporting based on water bills or operator statements. The permit-listed facility total of 27 emergency generators is retained, distinct from installation and operation. The City authorized four 6,000-gallon diesel tanks in July 2025; a later fuel-license amendment application filed September 8 was withdrawn October 13, so no additional capacity is inferred. Licensed tank capacity is not fuel inventory or use and the vocabulary has no matching storage-capacity metric. AP reports an operator-stated summer peak of about 118,000 gallons per day, but no meter ledger or annual total was published and the vocabulary has no direct actual peak-water metric. A Markley solar PPA covers a broader company purchase in Eversource territory and is not allocated to the National Grid-served Lowell site. No facility annual electricity, demand, tariff payment, grid-upgrade cost, verified annual water/wastewater, generator runtime, fuel use, actual emissions or selected-building resource series was found.

UMass Lowell lists Markley Group in the $25,000 Signature Sponsor tier for the Meehan Student Center dedication held May 1-2, 2026, providing a dated recipient-side amount. The University says the weekend raised more than $300,000 in total, but that event total is not attributed to Markley. Operator-side references to other local sponsorships and aggregate giving lacked matching recipient ledgers or defensible facility allocation and are not combined. project_updates.title: Structured-data and modeling audit — no defensible residual or county-effect model
project_updates.notes: Repository county economic panels for 2001-2024, study-county exclusions, inventory history and the direct evidence documented above were reviewed. The November 2015 operating anchor leaves a pre-period, but Markley is not Middlesex County's first known data-center operation: the repository's governed first-entry research documents earlier colocation activity in Somerville, and Markley itself had later 2018-2026 expansions that prevent a single stable treatment boundary. Newly retained permit estimates do not supply audited spending, labor coefficients or local-purchase shares, and the FY2026 billed-tax record has no same-scope marginal public-service cost. No project-specific construction payroll, supplier spending, operating payroll, annual resource quantity compatible with the evidence metrics or causal county outcome anchors were found. No construction, supplier, household, resource, fiscal-net, input-output, difference-in-differences, event-study, synthetic-control or descriptive county-comparison model is added; arbitrary transferred assumptions would create false precision rather than a bounded estimate. No records requests were made.
